newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall as poor sentiment remains.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall as poor sentiment remains.

text.p: Argentine bonds took another tumble early Wednesday as the market retained its depressed mode from recent days.
Traders said the market was still very jittery, adding that so far, despite the slump in recent days, there were no clear support levels.
"Investors are worried, the market is very nervous," said a trader at a large foreign bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.75 to 116.80, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 3/4 to 79-6/8.

Analysts at financial consultancy IDEA said in an investor note that former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo's charges against presidential chief of staff Alberto Kohan "added steam to the generalized sell-off in Argentine assets, and the damage is severe enough to weigh on the market for the next few days."
Cavallo reportedly told a judge that Kohan knew government officials had paid bribes to secure a deal between state-run Banco Nacion and U.S. computer giant IBM's local unit.
That accusation, in addition to other finger pointing by Cavallo at other government officials last week, has ruffled the market.
Even though these corruption accusations may not lead to anything concrete, "the fight between President Carlos Menem and Cavallo has the impression of being irreversible," said the trader.
